article_hits.content: Lego marketplace BrickLink offline after 'unusual activity' detected Image source, Reuters Image caption, The marketplace is sometimes called the 'eBay' of Lego By Zoe Kleinman Technology editor Published 28 minutes ago Lego has taken its online marketplace BrickLink offline after detecting what it described as unusual activity on the platform. BrickLink is used by Lego collectors worldwide to buy and sell secondhand Lego sets, source new bricks and purchase limited edition releases. It was originally set up by a fan, but Lego acquired it in 2019. In a homepage message, the firm said that before restoring BrickLink, it wanted to "fully understand" what had happened. "That means containing the issue, investigating how it happened and checking for related issues," Lego said. It did not provide any further detail about whether the site has been breached or hacked, and whether any customer data was affected. After being contacted by the BBC, Lego published the update. article_hits.title: Why are we still working this hard?
article_hits.content: Why Are We Still Working This Hard? In 1973, what a forty-hour week of work produced takes sixteen hours to produce today. That’s according to Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) input output tables. An hour of work in American business now makes two and a half times what it made in 1973. For every forty hours that used to be needed, twenty-four have been freed. You have probably not noticed them. The forty-hour week was written into American law by an act of 1938, and hasn’t changed. Counted for each head of population, the hours worked in American business in 2024 were 10 percent higher than in 1973. As a country, the US took the whole of fifty years’ progress as more output and none of it as time. It was supposed to go differently. article_hits.content: Andreeva wins 11 games in a row to thrash Sabalenka at WTA Finals Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mirra Andreeva beat Aryna Sabalenka in the 2025 Indian Wells final By Amy Lofthouse BBC Sport Senior Journalist Published 11 November 2026 Updated 42 minutes ago Mirra Andreeva won 11 games in a row as she thrashed world number two Aryna Sabalenka to reach the last four at the WTA Finals. The 19-year-old Russian went on to deliver a statement 6-4 6-0 victory over four-time major singles winner Sabalenka.
